content:
Apple is preparing for a more focused but potentially pricier iPhone launch this fall.

First, the more affordable base iPhone 18 will be pushed to spring next year. This means the September event will be headlined by the higher-priced Pro models and Apple's first foldable iPhone Ultra, with expected starting prices higher than ever.

Here's how Apple is laying the groundwork early to make this sticker shock easier to swallow for new customers and upgraders.

Apple Upgrade 低月費

First, Apple rolled out a new "Apple Upgrade" program in July, partnering with Klarna. Customers can choose to rent an iPhone for 12 or 24 months. Since the monthly fee only covers a portion of the device's price, it's lower than a traditional installment plan of the same length.

When the rental period ends, customers can choose to upgrade, return the iPhone, or pay the remaining balance to take ownership. AppleCare is an additional add-on, but the "Apple Care One" package can make the coverage bundle more cost-effective.

"Apple Upgrade" lets Apple advertise the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra with a more palatable monthly figure. This matters because rumors suggest one of these phones could carry a price tag as high as $2,500, rivaling a MacBook Pro.

Apple 調高 iPhone 以舊換新價值

Next, Apple has just raised trade-in valuations for most of its lineup.

The iPhone 16 Pro Max now nets up to $720, up from $695. The iPhone 16 Pro sees a bigger jump, from $560 to $630.

Customers can apply that credit toward either a traditional purchase or the "Apple Upgrade" rental program. So higher trade-in values further reduce the monthly cost.

Once the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra officially launch in September, Apple should also accept trade-ins of existing iPhone models.

Apple 擴大 Android 以舊換新適用範圍

Finally, Apple is reaching out directly to Android users. The updated list adds more Google, Samsung, and OnePlus models, including the Pixel 9 series, Galaxy S21 Ultra, OnePlus 13, and OnePlus 13R.

These users can likewise apply trade-in credit toward a purchase or the "Apple Upgrade" rental program. In other words, Apple is widening the funnel into its ecosystem just as its new devices push deeper into premium territory.

None of this makes the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Ultra cheap, but it lowers the visible monthly cost, boosts the value of older devices, and opens the door for more Android users to come in.

Taken together, these changes may help Apple sell what could be its most expensive iPhone launch ever. For customers who want to upgrade but balk at the high price tags, the standard iPhone 18 and a more affordable iPhone 18e are expected to arrive around March or April next year.
